t: Reformat Phone Number: Clean, Chunk in Threes, Handle the Tail
o:
## Understanding the problem

First delete every space and dash, keeping only digits. Then emit blocks left to right: take blocks of 3 digits while **more than 4** remain; the final 2, 3, or 4 digits become one block of 2, one of 3, or two blocks of 2. Join blocks with dashes. The output therefore never contains a 1-digit block and never more than two 2-digit blocks.

**Example 1:** "1-23-45 6" cleans to "123456" (6 digits): take 123, then 3 remain -> 456; result "123-456".

**Example 2:** "123 4-567" cleans to "1234567" (7 digits): take 123, then 4 remain -> split as 45-67; result "123-45-67".

The cleaned string has at most 20 characters (constraints give 2-20 including separators), so any linear scan fits; the only trap is the tail when exactly 4 digits remain.
k: Strip to digits first — separators carry no information, and the cleaned length drives every block decision.
Take 3-digit chunks only while MORE than 4 digits remain; tails of 2/3/4 map to xx / xxx / xx-xx.
The 4-digit tail is the sole case producing two 2-blocks separated by a dash inside the tail.

a.n: Approach 1: Strip Separators, Then Chunk in Blocks of 3
a.i: Filter the digits into one string, greedily slice off 3-digit chunks while more than 4 digits remain, then apply the tail rule to whatever is left (2, 3, or 4 digits, with 4 split into two pairs). Collect blocks in a list and join with dashes.
s: Remove all spaces and dashes to get digit string d.
While d has more than 4 digits, emit d[0:3] and drop it.
If exactly 4 digits remain, emit two blocks of 2; otherwise emit what remains as one block.
a.t: O(n) — each character is filtered once and placed into exactly one block
a.sp: O(n) — the cleaned string and block list

a.n: Approach 2: Single Pass with Position-Based Dash Placement
a.i: Compute the total digit count up front, then stream the answer character by character: after placing digit p (1-indexed), decide arithmetically whether a dash belongs here. When the total is not 1 mod 3, dashes follow every multiple of 3. When it is (the xx-xx tail case), dashes follow multiples of 3 up to the tail start plus one dash exactly two positions before the end.
s: Collect digits; let total be their count and special = (total mod 3 == 1).
Append digits in order; after digit p, stop when p equals total.
If special: append a dash when (p mod 3 == 0 and p <= total - 4) or p == total - 2.
Otherwise append a dash whenever p mod 3 == 0.
a.t: O(n) — one pass to filter digits, one pass to emit the result
a.sp: O(n) — the digit buffer and output builder

w:
## Wrap-up

Use Approach 1 in an interview — it is short, obviously correct, and easy to test by heart on lengths 2..8; quote Approach 2 only as a streaming variant if asked not to materialize blocks.

Common pitfalls:

- Emitting a 3-digit chunk when exactly 4 digits remain, stranding a lone final digit ("1234567" must become "123-45-67", never "123-456-7").
- Forgetting inputs may end in separators, or that the cleaned length can be as small as 2.
- Off-by-one in the tail condition: "more than 4" must be strict.

Follow-ups: generalize to arbitrary block patterns via a lookup table of tail formats, or batch-format many numbers sharing one compiled regex.
